- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.33), model often overshoots downward; avoid sharp drops; cap forecast below 0.5x recent low if sentiment persists.
- After a spike in model forecast (e.g., >3x recent mean), apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1.5–2x the spike magnitude for next 3–5d.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model is overconfident; use 30d moving average as baseline, not 30d forecast.
- For 30d horizon, if model forecast > 2x recent 7d high, flag as “overshoot” and reduce by 50% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and model forecast is high, assume “mean reversion bias”; apply 10–20% downward adjustment for next 10d.
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is low, consider “sentiment lag” — model underreacts; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3d.
